activity_overrides.reason: Malik-Shah I's 1072-1092 reign is the reviewed period in which Isfahan served as the principal Seljuk capital/court anchor. This exact Activity override closes the post-1072 place-function gap without converting the transregional Great Seljuk polity into a static leaf.
source_refs: Encyclopaedia Iranica: MALEKŠĀH — Isfahan can be considered the Seljuq capital during Malik Shah's reign
Encyclopaedia Iranica: NEẒĀM-AL-MOLK — vizier under Alp Arslan and Malik Shah until 1092

activity_overrides.reason: Tughril Beg's 1040-1063 rule used successive Iranian court centers rather than one fixed capital: Nishapur after the 1040 conquest, Ray from the early 1040s, and Isfahan from about 1050. All reviewed centers resolve to the same ATLAS Iranian-plateau leaf, so one exact Activity-level leaf binding preserves the spatial fact without inventing a permanent single capital.
source_refs: Encyclopaedia Iranica: CAPITAL CITIES — after Nishapur in 1040, Great Seljuk capitals shifted to Ray and then Isfahan
Encyclopaedia Iranica: ISFAHAN — Tughril moved his possessions to Isfahan around 1050 as a permanent residence
Encyclopaedia Iranica: KĀKUYIDS — Tughril came to Ray in the early 1040s and made it his capital for the following years
